# `hs-run review` — state map

<!-- generated by render_state_map.py — edit the SSOT, # learn: "${HARNESS_BIN_ROOT:-.}"/harness/data/hs-run-registry.d/<domain>.yaml, not this file -->

Every state `hs-run review` can report, with what it means. Run the CLI, read the `state`, do the judgment that state names, run it again — each state is re-derived from artifacts on disk, so deleting an artifact regresses the state.

This file is generated. Change the source named in the comment above, then re-render with `render_state_map.py`; edits made here are lost on the next render.

## States that route something

The CLI hands these rule and reference paths over at the moment the step begins — the body does not repeat them.

| state | what it means | routes |
|---|---|---|
| `needs_architecture_review` | The pending diff is structural — it adds or removes a module, changes an import edge, or touches a file the graph cannot read that standards.yaml calls structural. Judge it against the component map and layer boundaries, and record architecture_review{checked, doc_sha, drift[]} in the review-decision — the pr/ship gate refuses the plan without it. | `architectural-constraints`, `docs/system-architecture.md` |
| `ready` | The diff is prepared and ONE reviewer judges it in a single pass. The envelope carries the scope, the rules that govern these exact files, and the risk tier. | `claim-verification`, `anti-tautology-detection` |
| `ready_recall` | Same prepared diff, but effort is medium or higher, so the review fans out to subagents. Orchestration comes before any spawn; the recall ladder produces the findings; the verdict, gate and dismissals path are unchanged. | `orchestration-protocol`, `references/recall-mode.md` |
| `stuck` | This domain has answered the same thing enough times in a row that repeating it is no longer an attempt. Stop re-running and spawn `hs:escalation-consultant` for counsel — hand it the task, the evidence as file:line, what was already tried, and the specific question. It advises; the decision stays here. | `orchestration-protocol`, `agent-operational-discipline` |

## States that route nothing

Not a gap: each is fully served by the `next_action` line the envelope already carries, and needs no extra file to act on.

| state | what it means |
|---|---|
| `wrong_door` | The argument names a PR, a commit, or the whole codebase — all history questions. This verb reads the WORKING TREE and would answer about a different diff. `review_recall.py --effort <level>` serves those modes. |
| `git_diff_failed` | git could not answer, so there is no diff and no review. The envelope's warnings carry the repair; a review rule cannot help with a broken repository. |
| `nothing_changed` | The working tree has nothing to judge. The run is over at exit 0. |
| `codemap_offer` | This step reads code facts and the repo has no code map yet. Ask the user once; either answer ends the offer for this session, then run the step again and take its real answer (it is kept in `deferred`). |
| `facts_stale` | The code-graph snapshot backing this diff's `code.tests_reached`/ `code.importers`/`code.fan_in` facts is missing or older than HEAD within its own roots — run the named refresh command, then retry. The review's own projection (`domain_state`) is preserved underneath. |
